meta.disclaimer: Health summaries are for trip planning only. Consult a travel-health clinic or your doctor for personalised medical advice, vaccinations, and malaria prophylaxis.

vaccinations.title: Travel vaccinations — discuss with a clinic 6–8 weeks before departure

recommended.name: Hepatitis A
recommended.note: Recommended for most safari and self-catering trips — food and water exposure.

recommended.name: Typhoid
recommended.note: Advised for adventurous eaters and long rural stays.

recommended.name: Hepatitis B
recommended.note: Consider for extended travel or medical volunteering.

recommended.name: Tetanus / diphtheria
recommended.note: Ensure boosters current — bush camps and minor injuries.

recommended.name: Rabies
recommended.note: Consider for remote camping, bat caves, or long stays — pre-exposure series available.

tripSpecific.name: Yellow fever
tripSpecific.note: Required only if arriving from endemic countries — see routing rules below. Zambia is a risk country; certificate may affect onward travel.

tripSpecific.name: Malaria prophylaxis
tripSpecific.note: Essential for Luangwa, Okavango, Mozambique coast, and most lowveld summer travel — clinic chooses regimen.

tripSpecific.name: Cholera
tripSpecific.note: Rarely required for tourists; outbreaks occasionally affect urban areas — follow WHO alerts.

checklist: Travel insurance with medical evacuation (Medivac to Johannesburg or Nairobi)
Personal malaria meds plus DEET repellent and long sleeves at dusk
Copy of vaccination record and prescription medicines in original packaging
Antidiarrheal and rehydration salts for remote drives
Sun protection — UV extreme at altitude and in Namibia

yellowFeverRouting.title: Yellow fever certificate — when you need it
yellowFeverRouting.summary: Southern Africa does not require yellow fever vaccination if you fly directly from Europe, UK, or North America. A certificate becomes mandatory when you enter from or transit through yellow-fever endemic countries in the last 6–10 days (country rules vary).

rules.scenario: Direct flight from UK/EU/US to Johannesburg or Windhoek
Arriving from Kenya, Uganda, DRC, or Nigeria
rules.requirement: Valid yellow fever certificate mandatory — checked at immigration
Certificate required if departing endemic areas within 6 days — carry WHO booklet
Not required from non-endemic origins; Zambia is endemic — some countries require cert on return home

rules.scenario: Transit under 12 hours in endemic airport
rules.requirement: Rules vary — some countries exempt airside transit; confirm with airline and destination

yellowFeverRouting.note: South Africa enforces certificate checks strictly at OR Tambo when arriving from endemic countries. Get vaccinated at an authorised clinic at least 10 days before travel.

countries.name: South Africa
countries.malariaSummary: Low risk in most tourist areas. Risk exists in northeastern Limpopo and Mpumalanga (Kruger fringe) and northern KwaZulu-Natal — especially Nov–May.
countries.yellowFever: Certificate required if arriving from a yellow-fever endemic country within the past 6 days.
otherRisks: Sun exposure at altitude and coast

zones.notes: Prophylaxis sometimes advised Nov–May — ask your doctor.
Higher risk in summer rainy season.

countries.name: Namibia
countries.malariaSummary: Low in central and coastal areas. Moderate risk in the north (Etosha fringe, Kavango, Zambezi/Caprivi) during rainy season Nov–Jun.
countries.yellowFever: Certificate required if entering from endemic countries.

zones.notes: Standard repellent sufficient for most visitors.

countries.name: Botswana
countries.malariaSummary: Risk in northern Botswana (Okavango, Chobe, Moremi) year-round, peaking Nov–Apr. Low in Gaborone and Kalahari south.
countries.yellowFever: Required if travelling from endemic areas.
otherRisks: Hippos and crocs — follow guide instructions

zones.notes: Urban and southern routes generally safe.

countries.name: Zambia
countries.malariaSummary: Malaria present throughout including Victoria Falls and all major safari areas. Prophylaxis recommended for most visitors.
countries.yellowFever: Risk country — vaccination may be required depending on your travel history.
otherRisks: Bilharzia in Lake Kariba and river systems

zones.notes: Year-round risk; peak in rainy season.
Urban risk lower than valleys but not zero.

countries.name: Zimbabwe
countries.malariaSummary: Risk in Victoria Falls, Zambezi Valley, Hwange (summer), and Mana Pools. Lower in Harare and highveld.
countries.yellowFever: Certificate required from endemic transit countries.
otherRisks: Cash economy — carry USD small notes

countries.name: Mozambique
countries.malariaSummary: High risk nationwide including Maputo, coast, and Gorongosa. Prophylaxis recommended for essentially all visits.
countries.yellowFever: Vaccination certificate required for travellers from endemic countries.
otherRisks: Road travel at night not advised

zones.notes: Use nets and repellent even in beach lodges.

countries.name: Malawi
countries.malariaSummary: Risk throughout the country including Lilongwe and Lake Malawi shore. Prophylaxis recommended year-round.
countries.yellowFever: Required if arriving from endemic countries.
otherRisks: Bilharzia in lake shallows and reedy bays
Lake swimming — ask locally about safe beaches

zones.notes: Combine prophylaxis with repellent at dusk.
Cooler altitude reduces but does not eliminate risk.

countries.name: Lesotho
countries.malariaSummary: Very low malaria risk due to altitude. Main health concerns are altitude, cold exposure, and road safety on mountain passes.
countries.yellowFever: Required only if entering from endemic countries.

zones.notes: 4x4 required; check pass open status in winter.

countries.name: Eswatini
countries.malariaSummary: Low risk in most areas. Lowveld reserves (Hlane, Mkhaya) have moderate seasonal risk Nov–Apr.
countries.yellowFever: Required if arriving from endemic countries.
